Abstract
Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LAC) comprises a substantial subset of
non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnoses, where epidermal growth factor
receptor (EGFR) mutations play a pivotal role as indicators for therapeutic inter-
vention with targeted agents. The emerging ﬁeld of radiomics, which involves
the extraction of numerous quantitative attributes from medical imaging, when
coupled with positron emission tomography/ computed tomography (PET/CT)
technology,has demonstrated promise in the prognostication of EGFR mutation
status. The objective of this investigation is to construct and validate predictive
models for EGFR mutations in LAC by leveraging PET/CT-derived radiomics
features, thereby reﬁning diagnostic precision and facilitating tailored treatment
strategies.
Purpose: The aim of this study was to develop a non-invasive radiomics model
based on PET/CT with excellent performance for predicting the EGFR mutation
status in LAC. Thus, it can provide the basis for the individualized treatment
decision of patients.
Methods: Positron emission tomography (PET), computed tomography (CT),
clinical and pathological data of 112 patients with LAC admitted to our hospital
from January 2019 to June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. This research
cohort encompassed 54 LAC patients with EGFR wild type and 58 LAC patients
with EGFR mutated type.The participants were randomly assigned to the train-
ing group (n = 78) and the validation group (n = 34) in a 7:3 ratio.A sum of 3562
radiomics attributes were derived from PET/CT scans. The minimal absolute
shrinkage and selection operator method was employed to identify 13 notable
features. Based on these characteristics, support vector machine (SVM), gra-
dient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF) and extreme gradient
boosting (XGBOOST) were constructed. The forecasting effectiveness of the
model was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic
(ROC) Curve, the DeLong test, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
Results: SVM performance in PET/CT radiomics model was higher than that
of other machine learning models (training group areas under the curve [AUC]
of 0.916 and validation group AUC of 0.945, respectively). The integration of
radiomics and clinical data did not yield a superior predictive performance com-
pared to the radiomics model alone in terms of estimating EGFR mutation status
(AUC:0.916 vs.0.921,0.945 vs.0.955,p> 0.05,in both the training and validation
groups).
Conclusions: The SVM model has emerged as a commendable non-invasive
technique, showing high precision and dependability in forecasting EGFR

INTRODUCTION
Lung cancer is the second most prevalent cancer world-
wide, with one of the highest mortality rates, peaking
at 21%.1,2 Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) con-
stitutes around 85% of all lung cancer diagnoses and
is the predominant type leading to mortality from this
disease.3 Lung adenocarcinoma (LAC),the predominant
variant of NSCLC, is notable for its elevated frequency
of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations
compared to other subtypes.4 Our comprehension of
LAC’s molecular biology has substantially grown in
recent years. EGFR gene mutations are among the
most studied genetic changes in LAC, and adenocarci-
noma tumors with these mutations demonstrate higher
heterogeneity.5,6 Among Asian individuals afﬂicted by
LAC, EGFR mutation rates can reach up to 50%.7
Research contends that tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs)
can yield favorable outcomes for patients with LAC. A
study conducted by Bergqvist and peers revealed that
EGFR TKI therapy led to a median overall survival (OS)
of 15.5 months, with 1-year and 3-year survival rates
of 62% and 15%, respectively.8 In contrast, a median
OS of 5.7 months was observed for patients who did
not receive EGFR TKIs treatment, with corresponding
1-year and 3-year survival rates of 27% and 7%,respec-
tively. Consequently, TKIs are widely utilized for targeted
LAC therapy.9,10 Therapeutics and prognosis for LAC
are considerably inﬂuenced by patient-speciﬁc EGFR
mutations, signifying the importance of precise EGFR
mutation detection in these individuals for improved
prognosis.
Currently, EGFR mutations in LAC are identiﬁed
through
genetic
testing
post-biopsy. However, this
method can be time-consuming, invasive and its accu-
racy can be compromised by tumor heterogeneity.11,12
Therefore, the development of noninvasive, effective
techniques to predict EGFR mutations in LAC is neces-
sary. 18F-ﬂuorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomog-
raphy (18F-FDG PET/CT) proves useful in diagnosing
LAC, determining clinical staging, evaluating efﬁcacy,
and predicting prognosis.13 It monitors disease pro-
gression and, unlike computed tomography (CT) which
mainly focuses on anatomical imaging, positron emis-
sion tomography / computed tomography (PET/CT)
combines anatomical with functional imaging to detect
metabolic activity of tissues and organs with high sen-
sitivity. The lack of metabolic information in CT might
impact diagnosis accuracy and its ability to detect
small lesions is relatively poor. On the other hand, 18F-
FDG PET/CT has high sensitivity and speciﬁcity for
smaller lesions allowing early detection. Furthermore,
it aids in the evaluation of the systemic condition of
the tumor, beneﬁcial for understanding the stage and
metastasis of the tumor. This can improve diagnos-
tic accuracy and assist with accurate diagnosis and
treatment planning.14,15
Radiomics, a technique involving the quantitative
assessment of tumors through extensive feature extrac-
tion from medical images, enhances prognostic, predic-
tive, and diagnostic accuracy by integrating data into
clinical decision support systems.16 Studies show that
clinical factors such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA),
gender, and smoking history are signiﬁcantly associ-
ated with EGFR mutation status.17 While incorporating
these factors into a model can improve its predictive
accuracy, whether the addition of clinical parameters
can enhance a radiomics model’s performance remains
uncertain.18,19 In the present investigation, the exam-
ination was limited to adenocarcinoma, resulting in a
more focused research approach. Utilizing radiomics,
this investigation aimed to forecast EGFR mutation sta-
tus in LAC. The constructed radiomics model exhibited
robust predictive prowess, with the areas under the
curve (AUC) for EGFR mutation status prediction reg-
istering at 0.916 and 0.945 in separate evaluations.
The goal is to analyze its clinical application value and
establish a foundation for personalized treatment deci-
sion making in LAC patients, thus potentially improving
patient prognosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS
2.1
Patient cohort
Patient data: A total of 112 patients with LAC who had
undergone 18F-FDG PET/CT scans at our institution
between January 2019 and June 2023 were included
in this retrospective analysis. These patients were
treated in the First Afﬁliated Hospital of Nanchang
Medical College. The reviewed data has been ofﬁcially
veriﬁed. This research project was sanctioned by the
Ethical Review Board of the First Afﬁliated Hospital

for obtaining informed consent. This research group
encompassed 54 LAC patients with negative EGFR
gene tests and 58 LAC patients with positive EGFR
gene tests.The criteria for exclusion were as follows:(1)
without detection of EGFR mutations, (2) without com-

of EGFR mutations, (4) with other maglinant tumos,
and (5) without signiﬁcant metabolism. The participants
were randomly assigned to the training group and the
validation group in a 7:3 proportion. The training group
was utilized to train the predictive model, while the
cases in the separate validation group were employed
to assess the model’s efﬁciency.
2.2
Clinical data collection
Demographic information was obtained from patients’
medical records, including sex, age, smoking history,
tumor clinical stage, CEA. In addition, two nuclear
medicine physicians, both chest specialists with exten-
sive expertise in PET/CT diagnosis of LAC and no
knowledge of pathological diagnosis,each documented
two imaging features and a metabolic signature. It
included lesion involvement range, maximum major
axis diameter (MLD), maximum standard uptake value
(SUVMAX) (Table 1).
2.3
Examination methods
Cases were screened according to the above inclusion
and exclusion criteria, and those who met the criteria
were included in the study. 18F-FDG PET/CT images
were obtained using a Discovery STE PET/CT scanner
(GE HealthCare Technologies Inc., Chicago, IL USA) at
the First Afﬁliated Hospital of Nanchang Medical Col-
lege. Spiral CT scanning parameters: 120 kV, automatic
15∼180 mA, pitch 1.75, speed 0.8 s/ r, slice thickness
3.75 mm;PET scan parameters:2.5 min/ bed,6–8 beds,
slice thickness 3.75 mm. Images after attenuation cor-
rection and iterative reconstruction were transmitted to
AW4.6 workstation for PET image and CT image fusion,
and axial, coronal and sagittal images of patients were
reconstructed.18F-FDG was produced by our center and
synthesized by Tracerlab FXFN synthesizer with radio-
chemical purity > 95% and dosage: 0.10 ∼0.15 mCi/
kg. The scanning process extended from the scalp to
the upper third of the femur, with the patient being posi-
tioned in a supine posture. Before the examination, all
patients fasted for more than 4–6 h and measured their
height, weight, and fasting blood glucose. The blood
glucose should be controlled below 11.1 mmol/ L,prefer-
ably below 8.0 mmol/ L. If the blood glucose is too
high, hypoglycemic drugs or insulin injection can be
taken to control the blood glucose. The patient was then
instructed to rest in bed in a quiet rest room for 40 to
60 min, during which those who could drink water drank
400 mL–500 mL half an hour before bed, removed all
metal objects on the body, and emptied urine before
examination. The equipment utilized for the production,
synthesis, and inspection of
18F-FDG comprises the
GE MINIstrance cyclotron, Tracerlab FX chemistry auto
synthesizer, and discovery STE. The acquisition param-
eters for the 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging procedure are
detailed as follows (Table S1).
2.4
EGFR mutational status
Cellular samples from patients diagnosed with lung
cancer are collected through biopsy or surgical extrac-
tion. Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) represents an
advanced, high-capacity approach to genomic analy-
sis, facilitating swift and precise identiﬁcation of genetic
alterations. This innovative technique serves as a pow-
erful tool for genetic screening.It involves the isolation of
DNA from formalin-ﬁxed, parafﬁn-embedded samples,
followed by the creation of a targeted gene library,which
is then subjected to sequencing on state-of-the-art high-
throughput equipment. This process culminates in the
detailed examination of speciﬁc genetic mutations.
2.5
Region of interest segmentation
Two nuclear medicine physicians who have been
engaged in chest imaging diagnosis for more than 10
years used the Darwin Research Platform20 to manu-
ally sketch Region of interest (ROI) including all aspects
of the lesions along the edges of CT and PET images,
respectively, without knowing the pathological results
interest, different opinions at the same time consult
the superior doctor to decide. Then, the sketched map
was imported into Darwin laboratory (Yizhun Medical
AI Co. Ltd., Beijing, China) to extract radiomics features
(Figure 1).
2.6
Feature dimension reduction
The Min-Max normalization method and the Least
Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)
algorithm are employed to decrease the dimensional-
ity of the extracted image characteristics. Subsequently,
the Spearman correlation analysis method is utilized
to eliminate redundancy. Features with a high correla-
tion coefﬁcient (> 0.9) with other features are discarded,
resulting in meaningful characteristics derived from CT
and PET images, which are prepared for subsequent
modeling.

tion (the default parameter in the Feature Class Level).

2.8
The construction of radiomics
signatures
Four machine learning models, namely support vec-
tor machine (SVM), gradient boosted decision tree
(GBDT), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient
boosting (XGBoost), were constructed using the fea-
tures extracted from CT, PET, and PET/CT images. The
predictive performance of the models was assessed
using an independent validation group, which employed
the identical threshold dataset from the training group.
The accuracy of the models was validated through a
10-fold cross-validation approach. In the 10-fold cross-
validation process, each patient was utilized for both
training and validation. Performance evaluation of the
models was conducted using Receiver Operating Char-
acteristic (ROC) curves and AUC analysis (Figure 5).

2.9
Development of the combined
radiomics model
The clinical model was developed using the training
data set and logistic regression analysis. The clinical
model was constructed based on clinicopathological
factors related to EGFR (gender and smoking history;
p < 0.05).The AUC values for the training and validation
groups were 0.706 and 0.664, respectively. To estab-
lish a clinically applicable and more accurate model for
predicting EGFR mutations in LAC, we utilized the com-
bined PET/CT_SVM radscore model along with gender
and smoking history. The combination of the radiomics
and clinical models did not show a signiﬁcant advan-
tage over the radiomics model in predicting EGFR status
(AUC: 0.916 vs. 0.921, 0.945 vs. 0.955, in training and
validation groups) (Figure 6). According to the DeLong
test, no signiﬁcant statistical discrepancy was observed
between the radiomics model and the integrated model
(p > 0.05) (Table 3).
3
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS METHODS
We utilized a SVM algorithm for training purposes on
a designated dataset. SVM is recognized for their efﬁ-
ciency, strength, and resilience as a machine learning
classiﬁcation technique.21 Moreover, we constructed an
additional model that incorporated clinical attributes,
such as gender, smoking history, and lesion extent. We
combined radiomics features with clinical features to
examine their additive effect on classiﬁcation. The com-
bined model was built using logistic regression, which
amalgamated these distinct feature sets. The perfor-
mance of the classiﬁer was gauged by examining the
ROC curve.To comprehensively appraise the classiﬁer’s
efﬁcacy, we set the probability threshold equivalent to
the mutation prevalence to derive metrics including sen-
sitivity, speciﬁcity, positive predictive value, and negative
predictive value.
Statistical analysis was performed using R statistical
software (version 3.4.4). The Wilcoxon rank sum test
was employed for data with skewed distribution, while
the t-test was utilized for normally distributed data, to
analyze the probability scores of LAC with wild-type
EGFR versus those with mutated EGFR.The chi-square
test facilitated a comparative analysis between the two
datasets. To evaluate the predictive capabilities of the
models, metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, speciﬁcity,
positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and
the AUC value were computed.

RESULTS
4.1
Subject characteristics
This research involved 112 participants, who were
randomly assigned to either a training group (n = 78)
or a validation group (n = 34). Every participant had
distinct pathological ﬁndings, including 54 LAC patients
with EGFR-Wild type and 58 LAC patients with EGFR-
Mutated type. There were no signiﬁcant differences
in age, TNM, CEA, lesion involvement in the training
group. Nevertheless, notable disparities were present
with regards to gender and the history of tobacco use
between LAC patients with EGFR-Wild type and LAC
patients with EGFR-Mutated type in the training group.
4.2
Predictive performance of machine
learning models
Among the 12 machine learning models, PET, CT and
PET/CT machine learning models with the highest per-
formance were PET/CT_SVM. The AUC values for
CT_SVM, PET_SVM, and PET/CT_SVM in the train-
ing group were 0.855, 0.866, and 0.916, respectively. In
the validation group, the AUC values were 0.851, 0.803,
and 0.945 for CT_SVM, PET_SVM, and PET/CT_SVM,
respectively. The ROC curves for the three machine
learning models are displayed in Table 2 The perfor-
mance of the PET/CT_SVM model exceeded that of

DISCUSSION
Common gene mutations in LAC include EGFR, ALK
and ROS1, among others.24 Genetic testing of patients
generally enables lung cancer patients with gene muta-
tions to receive accurate and timely individualized
treatment while avoiding over-treatment of patients with-
out target mutations.25 Therefore, The development of
a noninvasive predictive model for EGFR mutations
in LAC is valuable. Numerous previous investigations
have illustrated the effectiveness of PET/CT radiomics
approaches in predicting EGFR mutation status in LAC.
Li et al.26 showed that integrating radiomics with clini-
cal and PET/CT imaging improved accuracy for EGFR
mutation prediction in LAC, with an AUROC of 0.882
and accuracy of 81.6% in training,and 0.837 with 74.1%
accuracy in validation.Xiao et al.27 applied the advanced
EfﬁcientNet-v2 model to PET/CT fusion scans for EGFR
mutation prediction,surpassing radiomics with AUROCs
of 83.64 and 82.41 in training, and accuracies of 81.92
and 80.62, respectively.
We developed a radiomics model using the RF algo-
rithm that performed well in predicting EGFR mutations
in invasive LAC, achieving AUC values of 0.916 and
0.945 in the training and validation groups, respec-
tively. Our ﬁndings indicate that our model outperforms
some previously published studies.28,29 This outcome
is rational given that our research employs a standard-
ized scanning protocol (utilizing slice thickness and the
same reconstruction algorithm). Signiﬁcant differences
in gender and smoking status were observed between
the EGFR-Wild type and EGFR-Mutated type groups,
prompting the inclusion of clinical risk factors in the
simple radiomics model to create a combined model.
However,there was no discernible discrepancy between
the performance of the radiomics model and the inte-
grated model,which contradicts previous studies.17,28,30
This discrepancy may be attributed to the near-identical
distribution of clinical characteristics between the EGFR
(+) and EGFR (−) groups in our research,making it chal-
lenging to differentiate between the two groups based
on clinical factors.
The main objective of this article is to utilize machine
learning techniques to develop a radiomics model,
based on 18F-FDG PET/CT scans, for predicting the
EGFR mutation status in patients with LAC.31 An
SVM-based PET/CT radiomics model was ultimately
chosen for this study, and it exhibited signiﬁcantly supe-
rior predictive performance compared to the clinical
model.32 The possible reason is that the radiomics
model can extract detailed features from a large number
of image data, including tumor morphology, structure,
texture, and so forth. These characteristics can reﬂect
tumor heterogeneity and provide additional informa-
tion for predicting EGFR mutation status.33 For speciﬁc
radiomics features in the model, the highest weight in
PET/CT_ SVM is wavelet-LHH_ﬁrstorder_mean, which
efﬁciently extracts texture information from images
and reﬂects the heterogeneity of pathological tissue,
a characteristic closely related to EGFR mutation
status.34

provides insight into the average voxel gray level within
a particular wavelet transformed domain (LHH level).
Wavelet transformation is known for its ability to dissect
signals across various scales and orientations, thereby
uncovering the texture and structural details within an
image.Consequently,the wavelet-LHH_ﬁrstorder_mean
feature likely indicates ﬂuctuations in the average gray
values of LAC tissue along these deﬁned orientations,
which may be linked to the EGFR mutation status.
Granata et al.36 found that the best performance in
distinguishing between dilation and tumor budding was
the wavet_LHL_ﬁrstorder_mean feature. Zhanget al.37
identiﬁed wavet_LHL_ﬁrstorder as the most signiﬁcant
radiomics feature in our study. This feature character-
izes differences in signal intensity, which is associated
with heterogeneity due to spinal cord demyelination,
cystic degeneration, and necrosis.
Radiomics models leverage sophisticated machine
learning
approaches,
including
SVM,
to
pinpoint
and integrate the most informative features, signiﬁ-
cantly enhancing their efﬁcacy in predicting clinical
outcomes.38 SVM stand out as a robust supervised
learning algorithm adept at handling complex, high-
dimensional datasets — making them particularly
well-suited for the analysis of the extensive radiomics
features
derived
from
medical
imaging.39,40
Their
capacity to navigate intricate and nonlinear relation-
ships between these features and the target variables
empowers SVM to uncover nuanced patterns that
might escape detection through conventional analytical
techniques.41
By employing kernel methods, SVM project the origi-
nal features into a higher-dimensional space,where they
can identify the most advantageous decision bound-
aries for class differentiation.42 This approach not only
boosts the model’s ability to generalize but also affords
it a valuable degree of resilience to outliers— critical
in the medical imaging domain, where data are fre-
quently marred by noise and artifacts.43 This robustness
ensures that the model remains stable and depend-
able even when confronted with less-than-ideal data,
enabling precise predictions despite the presence of
extraneous noise.
This study possesses high credibility and reliability
compared to previous studies since the sample size of
binary outcomes is almost evenly distributed (close to
1:1 ratio),making the ﬁndings suitable as a reference for
other studies and valuable for other researchers. There
are still some limitations in this study.First,this research
was conducted as a single-center retrospective analy-
sis,which might have been inﬂuenced by center-speciﬁc
factors and may not fully represent the entire patient
population. Secondly, the number of participants in this
investigation was comparatively limited, necessitating
further research with expanded cohorts to corroborate
our discoveries. Furthermore, the PET/CT system’s res-
olution and sensitivity play a pivotal role in the predictive
capabilities of the model. Superior resolution aids in
precisely demarcating tumor contours, thereby enhanc-
ing the precision of feature identiﬁcation. Enhanced
sensitivity, on the other hand, bolsters the detection of
radiopharmaceuticals and contributes to the robustness
of the model. Variations among different PET/CT sys-
tems may affect the model’s universality. Consequently,
future research ought to account for these discrepancies
and validate the model’s versatility through multi-center
trials.
6
CONCLUSION
The SVM model, utilizing PET/CT radiomics feature
analysis, has demonstrated notable precision and reli-
ability in its predictive outcomes. This indicates its utility
as a valuable diagnostic tool for determining EGFR
mutation status in LAC patients prior to therapy. The

Abstract: Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LAC) comprises a substantial subset of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnoses, where epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations play a pivotal role as indicators for therapeutic inter- vention with targeted agents. The emerging ﬁeld of radiomics, which involves the extraction of numerous quantitative attributes from medical imaging, when coupled with positron emission tomography/ computed tomography (PET/CT) technology,has demonstrated promise in the prognostication of EGFR mutation status. The objective of this investigation is to construct and validate predictive models for EGFR mutations in LAC by leveraging PET/CT-derived radiomics features, thereby reﬁning diagnostic precision and facilitating tailored treatment strategies. Purpose: The aim of this study was to develop a non-invasive radiomics model based on PET/CT with excellent performance for predicting the EGFR mutation status in LAC. Thus, it can provide the basis for the individualized treatment decision of patients. Methods: Positron emission tomography (PET), computed tomography (CT), clinical and pathological data of 112 patients with LAC admitted to our hospital from January 2019 to June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. This research cohort encompassed 54 LAC patients with EGFR wild type and 58 LAC patients with EGFR mutated type.The participants were randomly assigned to the train- ing group (n = 78) and the validation group (n = 34) in a 7:3 ratio.A sum of 3562 radiomics attributes were derived from PET/CT scans. The minimal absolute shrinkage and selection operator method was employed to identify 13 notable features. Based on these characteristics, support vector machine (SVM), gra- dient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBOOST) were constructed. The forecasting effectiveness of the model was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) Curve, the DeLong test, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: SVM performance in PET/CT radiomics model was higher than that of other machine learning models (training group areas under the curve [AUC] of 0.916 and validation group AUC of 0.945, respectively). The integration of radiomics and clinical data did not yield a superior predictive performance com- pared to the radiomics model alone in terms of estimating EGFR mutation status (AUC:0.916 vs.0.921,0.945 vs.0.955,p> 0.05,in both the training and validation groups). Conclusions: The SVM model has emerged as a commendable non-invasive technique, showing high precision and dependability in forecasting EGFR Med Phys. 2025;52:3697–3710. wileyonlinelibrary.com/journal/mp © 2025 American Association of Physicists in Medicine. 3697 3698 DENG ET AL. mutation statuses in individuals with LAC.
